title: Earnings Beat: Can Palantir sustain its explosive AI-driven growth? - Palantir raises outlook after blockbuster quarter | The Economic Times
text:
Palantir Technologies stunned Wall Street by delivering another quarter of explosive growth, fueled by surging demand for its artificial intelligence software from both government agencies and commercial customers. The company raised its full-year revenue forecast to $8.15 billion-$8.16 billion, up from its previous outlook of about $7.65 billion, after reporting second-quarter revenue of $1.94 billion, well ahead of analysts' expectations. The upbeat guidance sent Palantir shares soaring around 14% in after-hours trading. (Sources: Reuters, CNBC, The Wall Street Journal)

Palantir's second-quarter revenue surged 93% year-on-year as enterprises and governments accelerated AI deployments. The company reported adjusted earnings of 41 cents per share, comfortably beating market estimates. Operating margins also expanded sharply, reflecting improved profitability as AI software adoption scaled across industries, according to Reuters and market reports.

The company's U.S. government business continued to fire on all cylinders. Revenue from U.S. government customers climbed 90% year-on-year to $809 million, driven by rising demand for AI-powered defense and intelligence software amid increasing geopolitical tensions. Reuters reported that Palantir is also involved in the U.S. "Golden Dome" missile defense initiative alongside defense technology firms.

Palantir's commercial business delivered equally impressive momentum. U.S. commercial revenue jumped well into triple digits as companies expanded the use of Palantir's AI platform to automate operations and improve decision-making. Management also raised its forecast for U.S. commercial revenue this year to about $3.42 billion, highlighting strong enterprise adoption of generative AI applications, Reuters reported.

Chief Executive Alex Karp said businesses are increasingly seeking secure AI platforms that allow them to maintain control over sensitive data instead of relying entirely on external AI providers.

According to reports from Reuters and The Wall Street Journal, Palantir believes growing demand for secure, enterprise-grade AI solutions will remain a key driver of long-term growth as organizations prioritize data security and operational control.

Despite the strong domestic performance, Palantir continues to face hurdles overseas. Reuters reported that the company recently lost a French intelligence contract to a local competitor and is also facing legal scrutiny over a policing-related contract in London. International growth remains slower than its booming U.S. business, making domestic expansion the primary driver of earnings.

With another major guidance increase, investors will now focus on whether Palantir can sustain its extraordinary AI-driven growth. Analysts expect continued momentum from government contracts and enterprise AI adoption, while keeping an eye on international expansion and valuation after the sharp rally in the stock. Palantir's latest results reinforce its position as one of the biggest beneficiaries of the global AI spending boom.
